note: THE FIRST SHEET IN THIS CORPUS THAT REACHES CERMAK ROAD, and it was acquired for that one reason. Wright 1834, Hathaway 1834 and the Thompson 1830 plat all end on the School Section's south line, which is why data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut/terrain_spec.json held the South Branch at a constant easting below Twelfth Street from T-1149 until T-1150 and why `evidence_limit` sits at N -2149.4. This sheet covers North Avenue to below Thirty-First Street and the lake to Western Avenue -- a mile and a quarter past the terrain box's south wall -- and it draws the South Branch, the lake shore and the section grid over the whole of it. The 1821 GLO township plat of T39N R14E would be the better source and remains unreachable: glorecords.blm.gov answers 401 behind a login and an unattended run cannot fetch it (measured under T-1149 on 2026-09-15 and again under T-1150 the same day). GEOREFERENCED 2026-09-15 under T-1150: fourteen section corners of the Chicago mile grid -- State, Halsted, Ashland and Western against North Avenue, Chicago Avenue, Madison, Roosevelt, Cermak and Thirty-First -- matched to modern OpenStreetMap intersections in EPSG:26916, the same control method as wright_1834_gcps.json and thompson_1830_gcps.json, and fitted affine at RMS 25.0 m, max 35.7 m, 0.66 per cent axis-scale difference (data/traces/gcp/rees_rucker_1849_gcps.json). IT IS FOURTEEN YEARS LATE, and that is a real claim and not a rounding: what is read off it is the PLANFORM of a natural channel, and every work that straightened this reach is later than the sheet -- the Illinois & Michigan Canal (opened 1848) is drawn on it as a separate line meeting the river at Bridgeport, south of the box, and the South Branch's own straightening between Eighteenth and Twenty-Second is 1928-30. Nothing traced from it is written `documented`: the one trace taken so far, data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut/south_branch_below_twelfth.geojson, is INFERRED and lies entirely below `evidence_limit`, which writes it conjectural anyway. THE CROSS-CHECK: where this sheet's trace meets Wright's committed one, at N -2110, the two surveys put the channel's banks 6.1 m and 19.4 m apart on a fit whose own RMS is 25.0 m. The sheet is a FOLDED map and its creases are the strongest straight lines on it -- four fold columns and six fold rows, one of which crosses the South Branch and erases sixteen rows of it; the fold positions are recorded in the GCP file so they are never mistaken for survey lines. Nothing else on this sheet has been read: the pre-fill lake shore beside this reach is T-1151's and is not traced here.
